newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black business seeks new S.Africa mining stake.
newsitem.headline: Black business seeks new S.Africa mining stake.

text.p: South Africa's leading black company said Thursday it planned to take joint control of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd., the world's third- biggest gold producer, in a major boost for black business.
New Africa Investment Ltd. (Nail) aims to buy a 17.2 percent stake in the company in a deal worth more than 1.8 billion rand ($400 million) based on current market prices.
The stake would give New Africa shared control with Rembrandt Group Ltd., a conglomerate whose businesses range from tobacco to mining.
"The aim is to enter into a partnership with Rembrandt in the control of Gold Fields ... (but) discussions are still at a very preliminary stage," Nail Deputy Chairman Cyril Ramaphosa told Reuters.
The deal would mark black business' second major foray into the white-owned mining industry following the sale of a controlling stake in JCI Ltd. to a rival group earlier this year.
The deal was seen as benefiting both sides.

Mining analysts said Ramaphosa, a former secretary-general of the African National Congress and one-time leader of the National Union of Mineworkers, could be a catalyst for improving sometimes strained labour relations at Gold Fields.
They doubted any significant premium would be involved in the sale given that Nail was the only bidder.
Gold Fields shares have already outperformed the sickly Johannesburg gold share index by over 40 percent in the last year, spurred by persistent takeover talk.
Trevor Pearton, mining analyst at Societe General Frankel Pollak, said Rembrandt -- Gold field's largest shareholder -- was probably the main driver of the deal.
"I think Rembrandt felt they had to do something with Gold Fields. It has been a static investment for too long," he said.
Further down the line, Pearton said it was possible that Rembrandt, and perhaps another big shareholder, Liberty Life, would opt to surrender more of their shares.
But the negotiations for the 17.2 percent stake promise to be lengthy as Nail haggles for control of shares in two holding concerns that hold the key to the Gold Fields riches.

Nail aims to acquire from Gold Fields and its Driefontein Consolidated Ltd. unit their 40 percent shareholding in Asteroid Ltd. Asteroid holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd., which, in turn, holds 43 percent of Gold Fields.
Rembrandt already holds 40 percent of GFSA, while Liberty has 20 percent.
Gold Fields is a leading player in local and international markets but its earnings record has been patchy, adding to pressure on management for a major rethink of its structure.
